newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf signs oil exploration deal with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Elf signs oil exploration deal with Syria.

text.p: French oil firm Elf Aquitaine said on Thursday it had signed an exploration and production sharing contract with Syria, in a deal also involving Japan's Sumitomo and Malaysian state-owned oil company Petronas.
The contract, Elf's second in Syria, allows the partners to explore in an area of 4,200 square kilometres in the northern part of the country.
Syria produced 600,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil in 1995.

Elf said its Elf Hydrocarbures Syrie subsidiary would operate the permit with a share of 40 percent, with the remaining 60 percent divided equally between Sumitomo Petroleum Development Company Ltd and Petronas Carigali Overseas SDN BHD.
Under the deal, the Elf-led consortium will carry out modern three-dimensional seismic studies on 1,100 square kilometres and drill three exploration wells during three and a half years.

"This is the second permit in Syria for Elf and Petronas and the first for Sumitomo," Elf said. "Elf Aquitaine confirms with this new contract its willingness to develop its activities in Syria where its present operated production amounts to 60,000 barrels of oil a day."
The company also has Middle East operations in OPEC member Qatar and in Oman, which like Syria is outside the oil cartel.
